# Quick Study Guide: 5. Advanced Query Filtering, Projection & Pagination

> "A query filter narrows results to documents matching specific field values or query operators (e.g. $gt, $lt, $in). An empty filter ({}) matches every document. The second argument to find() is a projection, which controls which fields are included or excluded in the returned documents. Use 1 to include a field and 0 to exclude it. sort() orders the results of a find() query. Use 1 for ascending order and -1 for descending order on the given field. limit() caps the number of documents returned by a query. skip() omits a given number of documents from the start of the results — commonly combined for pagination."

## 1. Topic Executive Overview

This quick guide covers **5. Advanced Query Filtering, Projection & Pagination**. Use it before your exam for fast revision. It shows exact definitions, simple code, and tables.

## 5.1 Conditional Filter Operators

> "A query filter narrows results to documents matching specific field values or query operators (e.g. $gt, $lt, $in). An empty filter ({}) matches every document."

- **Relational Comparison: `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$ne`.** Place comparison operators inside curly braces after the field name. For example, write `{ age: { $gte: 18 } }`. Here, `$gt` means greater than and `$gte` means greater or equal. Also, `$lt` means less than, `$lte` means less or equal, and `$ne` means not equal.
- **Set Membership (`$in`, `$nin`) & Logical (`$or`, `$and`).** Use `$in` with a list in square brackets, like `{ age: { $in: [17, 18, 19] } }`. It matches any value inside that list. Conversely, `$nin` matches values not in the list. Use `$or` when at least one rule must be true. Use `$and` when all rules must be true.

```javascript
// 1. Greater than or equal to ($gte)
db.students.find({ age: { $gte: 18 } });

// 2. Match any value in a list ($in)
db.students.find({ age: { $in: [17, 18, 19] } });

// 3. Match if EITHER condition is true ($or)
db.students.find({
  $or: [{ age: { $gte: 19 } }, { name: "Rahul" }]
});
```

| Operator | Meaning | Simple Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `$gt` / `$gte` | Greater than (`>`) / Greater than or equal (`>=`) | `{ age: { $gte: 18 } }` |
| `$lt` / `$lte` | Less than (`<`) / Less than or equal (`<=`) | `{ age: { $lt: 20 } }` |
| `$ne` | Not equal (`!=`) | `{ grade: { $ne: 7 } }` |
| `$in` / `$nin` | In list / Not in list | `{ age: { $in: [17, 18, 19] } }` |
| `$or` / `$and` | Either rule true / Both rules true | `{ $or: [ { c1 }, { c2 } ] }` |

## 5.2 Field Projection Mechanics

> "The second argument to find() is a projection, which controls which fields are included or excluded in the returned documents. Use 1 to include a field and 0 to exclude it."

- **Inclusion Projection: Using `1` to Show Fields.** When you write `{ name: 1, age: 1 }` as the second argument of `find()`, MongoDB shows only `name`, `age`, and `_id`, while automatically hiding every other field.
- **Exclusion Projection & Hiding `_id` with `_id: 0`.** MongoDB always includes the `_id` field by default, even when you do not ask for it. To hide `_id`, you must explicitly write `_id: 0` inside your projection, like `{ name: 1, age: 1, _id: 0 }`.

```javascript
// Show only name and age for every student, and hide _id
db.students.find({}, { name: 1, age: 1, _id: 0 });

// Show only name and grade for every student, and hide _id
db.students.find({}, { name: 1, grade: 1, _id: 0 });
// Output: [ { name: "Aditi", grade: 8 }, { name: "Rahul", grade: 9 } ]
```

| Projection Code | What Is Shown | What Is Hidden |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `{ name: 1, age: 1 }` | `_id`, `name`, and `age` | All other fields |
| `{ name: 1, age: 1, _id: 0 }` | Only `name` and `age` | `_id` and all other fields |
| `{ subjects: 0 }` | Every field except `subjects` | Only `subjects` |

---

## 5.3 Cursor Pipeline Transformation & Pagination

> "sort() orders the results of a find() query. Use 1 for ascending order and -1 for descending order on the given field. limit() caps the number of documents returned by a query. skip() omits a given number of documents from the start of the results — commonly combined for pagination."

- **Result Ordering (`sort({ field: 1 | -1 })`).** You use `.sort({ age: 1 })` to sort from smallest to largest (ascending) and `.sort({ age: -1 })` to sort from largest to smallest (descending).
- **Offset Skipping (`skip(n)`) & Result Limiting (`limit(n)`).** You use `.skip(10)` to ignore the first 10 results and `.limit(5)` to return at most 5 results. When you chain `.sort({ age: 1 }).skip(10).limit(5)` together, you get a clean page of 5 ordered results!

```javascript
// 1. Sort students from highest to lowest age (-1 = descending)
db.students.find().sort({ age: -1 });

// 2. Pagination: sort by age (1 = ascending), skip first 10, return next 5
db.students.find().sort({ age: 1 }).skip(10).limit(5);
```

| Cursor Method | Example | What It Does |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `sort({ age: 1 })` | `1` or `-1` | Orders results ascending (`1`) or descending (`-1`) |
| `skip(10)` | Number of docs | Skips the first `10` documents |
| `limit(5)` | Number of docs | Returns at most `5` documents |

---

## Rapid Exam Trap Checklist

- The `_id` field is always shown by default. You must write `_id: 0` inside the projection to hide it.
- In `.sort({ age: 1 })`, `1` means ascending order (smallest to largest) and `-1` means descending order.
- When you combine `.sort()`, `.skip()`, and `.limit()`, MongoDB always runs `sort` first, `skip` second, and `limit` last.
